sentences.text: This Court by its order dated 19.1.2023 gave the following directions:- "As the dispute is matrimonial and the parties have arrived at a compromise and some of the sections involved are non-compoundable, hence the parties are directed to appear before the trial court along with the compromise deed within 15 days from today.

The trial court is directed to verify the compromise deed of the parties and pass an order thereon and transmit the certified copy of verified compromise deed along with the order passed thereon, to this court within 15 days thereafter.

Till the date of presenting compromise deed in the trial court, no coercive measure shall be taken against the applicant."
4.

From the perusal of the record, it transpires that an application for extension of time was moved,
which was allowed.
Thereafter, the compromise has been duly verified and a report has been filed to this Court.
Perusal of the record further indicates that Civil Judge (S.D.)/FTC, Meerut, has filed a report dated 15.3.2023, whereby the compromise in question has been verified.
The copy of the compromise as well as the order passed on the said compromise, recording the verification of the said compromise of the parties, is also available on the record.

5. Sri Rajendra Prasad Tiwari, Learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Vineet Tiwari, Learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 submit that dispute in question is a matrimonial dispute and the parties have now amicably settled their dispute.
A mutual divorce has been sought, which has been granted under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act.
This case was a case of no injury and Section 307 I.P.C. was also not attracted.

6. Sri Vineet Tiwari, Learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 further submits that once the parties have settled their matrimonial dispute amicably, continuation of the proceedings would tantamount to an abuse of the process of law.
He presses that proceedings be quashed to give quietus to the dispute between the parties.
7. Sri Shashi Dhar Pandey, Learned A.G.A. for the State-respondents could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

8. This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of:-
(i). B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675.

sentences.text: 9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose would be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned case.

10. Accordingly, the entire criminal proceedings pursuant to the charge sheet dated 09.04.2016 filed in Case Crime No.38 of 2016, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 307, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P.
Act, P.S. - Pallavpuram, District- Meerut as well as entire proceeding of the Criminal Case No.5189 of 2016 (State Vs. Rakesh Tyagi and Others), are hereby quashed.
